Maintenance Report — MNT-0195-010

Asset: WELL-0195 (NE-08 Well 195, T200, Northeast Block 8) Equipment: pump jack Work started: 06 Oct 2023 08:00 · Finished: 31 Oct 2023 15:00 · Well stopped for this job: 607 hours Crew lead: Megan Ward (U-305) · Crew: Daniel Foster Triggered by: inspection INS-0195-0050 on 2023-10-05 Report written: 01 Nov 2023

What happened

Field staff reported that the pump jack was running rough with a loud knock at the top of each stroke, so the operator stopped it. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0195-0050 showed the wellhead at 24.5 °C with the air at 22.8 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. A vibration check and visual inspection found play in the saddle bearing and scoring on the bearing housing. The well stayed shut in for about 23 days longer than the repair itself because the replacement part was back-ordered from the supplier.

Root cause

Bearing wear from long service and an overdue grease interval. This is corrective repair number 3 on this well's pump jack in the last 12 months.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).

Work done

  1. Lowered the horsehead and supported the walking beam with a crane.
  2. Removed the saddle bearing assembly.
  3. Cleaned the housing and checked alignment.
  4. Fitted a new saddle bearing and torqued the bolts to the manufacturer's values.
  5. Greased all structural bearings.

Summary of the fix: replaced saddle bearing and re-greased.

Testing and return to service

Ran the unit for 2 hours: smooth stroke, no knocking, bearing temperature normal. The well was returned to production.

What happened

Field staff reported that the separator was overfilling and the dump valve was not opening. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0195-0199 showed the wellhead at 35.6 °C with the air at 35.8 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. The level controller had failed. The well stayed shut in for about 2 days longer than the repair itself because heavy rain made the lease road impassable for the service truck.

Root cause

Controller float and switch failure.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 1 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).

Work done

  1. Isolated and depressurised the separator.
  2. Replaced the level controller.
  3. Calibrated the controller and tested the dump valve.

Summary of the fix: replaced level controller.

Testing and return to service

Cycled the separator three times; level control worked correctly. The well was returned to production.
